description: Held-out real vulnerable PRs: researched after the SQLi reviewer was developed on cases.json; scored once.

cases.title: Adding spatial lookups to RasterField interpolated the user-supplied band index from the lookup tuple straight into the PostGIS SQL template, so a non-integer band index injects SQL.
cases.where: PostGISOperator.check_raster() in postgis/operations.py: template_params['rhs'] = '%s, %s' % (template_params['rhs'], lookup.band_rhs) (and same for lhs); band_rhs comes unvalidated from self.rhs[1] in GISLookup.process_band_indices() in gis/db/models/lookups.py, e.g. filter(rast__contains=(rast, '<payload>')).
cases.notes: Fix 'Fixed CVE-2026-1207' (81aa529, on main) adds isinstance(int) checks right on the two interpolation lines in check_raster. git log -S on the 'Look for band indices and inject them' block shows it was introduced only by bbfad84 'Fixed #25588 -- Added spatial lookups to RasterField' (2016, on main). PR #5460 was closed and committed manually by a Django committer, so pr 5460 is the review PR but merge_commit is the single committed commit (single parent 03efa30). Old code (2016) but 2026 advisory.

cases.title: Reworking QuerySet.order_by() validation dropped the ORDER_PATTERN regex check for strings containing a period, so a 'table.column'-style value from request input is passed through as raw SQL in ORDER BY.
cases.where: Query.add_ordering() in django/db/models/sql/query.py: `if isinstance(item, str) and ORDER_PATTERN.match(item):` became `if isinstance(item, str):` and items with '.' now hit `continue` (deprecation warning only) without any validation, then reach the compiler as raw SQL.
cases.notes: The fix commit message names 513948735 as the regression ('Regression introduced in 513948735b...'). PR #12669 shows merged; merge_commit_sha equals 513948735 (rebase-merge, single parent 98ea4f0). Fix is the [3.2.x] backport a34a5f7 (in tag 3.2.5, which also contains 513948735); main was never fixed because the feature was removed there. Its diff re-adds ORDER_PATTERN and `if '.' in item and ORDER_PATTERN.match(item)` in query.py. Caveat: published in 2021, so higher training-data contamination risk.

cases.title: Adding min()/max()/sum()/avg() aggregates wrapped the caller-supplied column name in sqlalchemy.text() with no check that it is a real model field, so a crafted column string injects SQL into the aggregate query.
cases.where: SelectAction.get_text_clause() in queryset/actions/select_action.py returns sqlalchemy.text(f"{alias}{self.field_name}"); QuerySet._query_aggr_function() / min() / max() in queryset/queryset.py build select_actions from user column strings and only check is_numeric for sum/avg.
cases.notes: Advisory names commit ff9d412 as the origin; that commit is in PR #130 (true merge commit 61c456a, first parent e306eec). Confirmed the PR diff adds get_text_clause with sqlalchemy.text(f"...") and the min/max/_query_aggr_function methods. Fix PR #1557 (squash a03bae1, parent ef95d32) adds a field_name-in-model_fields check in _query_aggr_function in queryset.py; select_action.py is unchanged by the fix. ORM library for FastAPI/Starlette apps, not an app.

cases.title: Adding Lucene-style ?q= query string search for alerts made the Postgres backend build WHERE clauses by str.format()-ing user search terms into SQL.
cases.where: SearchTerm.__repr__() in postgres/parser.py returns e.g. '"{}" ILIKE \'%%{}%%\''.format(field, word) and '"{}"=\'{}\''.format(field, string); QueryBuilderImpl in postgres/utils.py does query = [repr(expression.parseString(params.get('q'))[0])] and puts it into the WHERE clause.
cases.notes: Advisory links both PRs. PR #712 squash commit aeba85a (parent cc0993d) adds parser.py and the utils.py q= sink. parser.py was later renamed to postgres/queryparser.py (in #714), so fix PR #2040 (squash fdd52cd, parent 71c098d) changes queryparser.py and utils.py. The fix diff touches utils.py at the same path; parser.py appears only under its new name.

cases.title: Adding epic order to user-story listings took the ?epic= query parameter and str.format()-ed it into a raw SQL subquery passed to queryset.extra(), enabling time-based blind SQL injection.
cases.where: attach_epic_order() in userstories/utils.py: sql = """... "epics_relateduserstory"."epic_id" = {epic_id}"""; sql = sql.format(tbl=..., epic_id=epic_id); queryset.extra(select={as_field: sql}); epic_id comes from self.request.QUERY_PARAMS.get("epic") in UserStoryViewSet.get_queryset() in userstories/api.py.
cases.notes: The advisory has no commit refs and gives the fixed version as 6.9.0, so I diffed 6.8.3..6.9.0. Fix 107f116b ('Force cast', pushed directly to main) changes only this line, to epic_id=int(epic_id). I traced the request flow: GET /api/v1/userstories?epic=<payload> -> attach_extra_info -> attach_epic_order. git blame puts every line of attach_epic_order, and the api.py epic param plumbing, in the single commit e2f6245 (2016, 66 py lines). That commit reached main inside the large epics PR #770, so introducing is the single commit. A sibling fix in the same release (2fca4e4c, timeline/service.py namespace) was left out because its inputs are not user-controlled. The advisory is a published repo advisory, but it is not in the global GHSA DB: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-chm9-9wwq-xffj returns 404, so advisory_url points at the repo advisory.

cases.title: Adding the external Postgres metadata plugin introduced FilterEngine.create_postgres_query(), which str.format()s DID-search filter keys and values from the REST API straight into raw SQL.
cases.where: FilterEngine.create_postgres_query() in did_meta_plugins/filter_engine.py: e.g. expression = "{}->>'{}' {} '{}'".format(jsonb_column, key, POSTGRES_OP_MAP[oper], value), plus the LIKE/boolean/float/timestamp branches; reached via GET /dids/<scope>/dids/search when postgres_meta is configured (postgres_meta.py, added in the same PR).
cases.notes: Advisory has no commit refs. Fix found in the master history of filter_engine.py: 5e15ae4, whose message says 'Advisory: GHSA-6j7p-qjhg-9947'. It adds a key allowlist regex and '' quote-escaping on the exact .format lines. It is a direct commit on master, no PR found. Follow-up f425a03 refactors to psycopg sql composition. Introducing PR #5649 (true merge 4313fdf, first parent fdcaebc) adds all 14 .format() expression lines. Caveats: 324 stars, below the 1k preference. Rucio is a scientific data-management service with a Flask REST API. It shares filter_engine.py with the next case.

cases.title: Porting the DID filter engine to JSON metadata added an Oracle branch that str.format()s user filter keys and values into a json_exists() expression wrapped in sqlalchemy text().
cases.where: FilterEngine.create_sqla_query() Oracle json-column branch in did_meta_plugins/filter_engine.py: expression = text("json_exists(meta,'$?(@.{} == \"{}\")')".format(key, value)); later split into like/boolean/numeric/string variants by #5567 with the same pattern.
cases.notes: Fix f997412 ('Advisory: GHSA-vjr5-c9qv-hgm3', direct commit on master) switches these lines to PASSING :val bindparams and adds a key allowlist. git blame at the fix's parent points to f2c83203 (#5567). That commit's diff shows it replaced an older injectable json_exists .format line, which git log traces to PR #5104 (squash 6b40362, first parent 81394b7; the PR API's base.sha 6cc6267 is the PR-time base). The vulnerable line is present in that diff. Oracle-only. Same file as the Postgres rucio case, but a distinct GHSA, introducing PR and fix commit.

cases.title: Adding transaction savepoints interpolated the caller-supplied savepoint name into SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO/RELEASE statements with f-strings.
cases.where: PostgresTransaction.savepoint() and Savepoint.rollback_to()/release() in engine/postgres.py (and the SQLite equivalents in engine/sqlite.py): await self.connection.execute(f"SAVEPOINT {name}") etc.
cases.notes: git blame of savepoint() at the fix's parent -> 72b8597 'Transaction savepoints (#778)', the squash merge of PR #778 (parent 021d782). The PR diff contains the f-string execute lines. Fix 82679eb ('Merge pull request from GHSA-xq59-7jf3-rjc6', a single-parent commit on master) adds validate_savepoint_name() and calls it in postgres.py and sqlite.py. Caveats: published 2023 (older), and the input is the savepoint name a developer passes in, which is a weaker web threat model. This is the weakest case; drop it first.

cases.title: PR #6490 moved structure-board rendering into a new generic render_object_structure admin endpoint and dropped the user_can_change_page check the old details() path applied, so any staff user can read the plugin structure of pages they may not view.
cases.where: cms/views.py: new render_object_structure(request, content_type_id, object_id) does content_type.get_object_for_this_type(pk=object_id) and renders cms/toolbar/structure.html with no permission check; the same diff deletes the old `if user_can_change_page(request.user, page) and structure_requested:` branch from details(). cms/admin/placeholderadmin.py registers it as ^object/([0-9]+)/structure/([0-9]+)/$.
cases.notes: Squash commit 0f12156 has a single parent 9f25075; PR #6490 targeted release/4.0.x (2018). Found via git log -S'def render_object_structure'. Fix 7642a98 (PR #8645, release/5.0.x, single parent 1b164a4) adds user_can_view_page() to render_object_structure in cms/views.py; the same fix also covers GHSA-4xfr-4p46-gc6p (clipboard). GHSA-8qj2-c6q4-f399 (non-PageContent branch, fix 9c82abf/PR #8703) has the same introducing change, so it is an alternative label for this diff, not a separate case. Old introducing code (2018) is a contamination risk.

cases.title: The billing PR added a PATCH /api/subscription endpoint that takes the target customer's email from a query parameter instead of the logged-in user, so any authenticated user can cancel or resume anyone's Stripe subscription.
cases.where: src/khoj/routers/subscription.py (new file): update_subscription(request, email: str, operation: str) under @requires(['authenticated']) calls stripe.Customer.list(email=email) and then stripe.Subscription.modify(..., cancel_at_period_end=True/False) with no check that email == request.user.object.email.
cases.notes: Merge commit 1d3bdf8 has parents cec54e3 (first) and a260997; PR #537 merged into the features/multi-user-support-khoj branch, which later reached master. git log -S'Customer.list(email=email' traces the pattern to commits inside this PR. The file was renamed to src/khoj/routers/api_subscription.py by commit 3bb1012 (same day) and the fix 47d3c8c (direct push, no PR, single parent d702710) edits the renamed file, replacing the email query param with request.user.object.email. Both paths are listed in vulnerable_files; the introducing diff touches the first, the fix the second.

cases.title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.
cases.where: src/sentry/api/endpoints/rule_snooze.py (new file): RuleSnoozeEndpoint.post(self, request, project, rule_id) does Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id) / AlertRule.objects.get(id=rule_id) without filtering by project, then creates a RuleSnooze for that rule.
cases.notes: Verified with a shallow fetch: both commits are single-parent squash commits. The fix's parent is ca59242c (the PR API's base.sha 2c4242ed is stale). The fix moves the lookup into convert_args with Rule.objects.filter(project=project) / AlertRule.objects.fetch_for_project(project). Between the two commits the file went through about 15 small refactors (a delete endpoint, a BaseRuleSnoozeEndpoint/get_rule helper), but the unscoped .objects.get(id=rule_id) appears in the introducing PR and survives unchanged in meaning.

cases.title: PR #54871 added a user notification-option DELETE endpoint that looks up the NotificationSettingOption by id without restricting it to the URL's user, so any user can delete other users' alert notification settings.
cases.where: src/sentry/api/endpoints/user_notification_options_detail.py (new file): UserNotificationOptionsDetailEndpoint.delete(self, request, user, notification_option_id) calls NotificationSettingOption.objects.get(id=notification_option_id) without user=user and deletes the result.
cases.notes: Verified with a shallow fetch: both commits are single-parent squash commits. The file was renamed to user_notification_settings_options_detail.py one day later (12f21f8, PR #54903) with a one-line change. The fix (PR #77093) edits the renamed path and adds user=user to the lookup. Both paths are listed in vulnerable_files.

cases.title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.
cases.where: authentik/enterprise/providers/ssf/views/stream.py: StreamView gains get(), patch(), put() and a rewritten delete() that call self.get_object() with no request.user.has_perm('authentik_providers_ssf.add_stream', self.provider) check, which sits right beside the existing post(); the new StreamVerifyView.post and StreamStatusView.get also have no check.
cases.notes: Single-parent squash commit. The fix PR #24064 is an automated backport of the security patch to main (single parent 2a324e9). It adds the has_perm check to get/patch/put/delete, StreamVerifyView.post and StreamStatusView.get/post. The fix commit's doc file is named GHSA-4r87-w2cx-fr3f.md (the draft id), but the published repo advisory is GHSA-hmrg-vpp4-gj88 (same text). It is not in the global advisory DB (authentik is not on PyPI), so advisory_url points to the repo advisory. Caveat: delete() existed unchecked since the original SSF PR #12327; the advisory says 2026.2 exposed only deletion. This PR introduced the read/update/verify/status exposure (2026.5). StreamStatusView.post came later (PR #21521).

cases.title: The Timeline revamp PR added IssueBulkUpdateDateEndpoint, which fetches issues by caller-supplied ids without filtering by the URL's workspace and project, so a member of any project can change start/target dates of any issue on the instance.
cases.where: apiserver/plane/app/views/issue/base.py: new IssueBulkUpdateDateEndpoint.post(self, request, slug, project_id) under @allow_permission([ROLE.ADMIN, ROLE.MEMBER]) does `issues = list(Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids))` and bulk-updates start_date/target_date.
cases.notes: Found with git log -G on the exact line; single-parent squash commit. The directory was renamed apiserver/ -> apps/api/ in 2025 (#7321/#7342); the fix (PR #8834, single parent 00a51f5) is a one-line change adding workspace__slug=slug, project_id=project_id. It is not in the global advisory DB (Plane is not on PyPI), so advisory_url is the repo advisory.

cases.title: PR #36990 added the support app's CourseTeamManageAPIView with only IsAuthenticated, without the support-role gate every sibling support view uses, so any learner can probe arbitrary accounts and instructors can read other users' course roles.
cases.where: lms/djangoapps/support/rest_api/v1/views.py (new file): class CourseTeamManageAPIView(GenericAPIView) with permission_classes = (IsAuthenticated,); get() resolves an arbitrary target user from the email/username/user_id query params (404 vs 200) and returns that user's staff/instructor roles over the caller's accessible courses.
cases.notes: The repo was renamed edx-platform -> openedx-platform (the API redirects). The advisory itself names PR #36990 as the origin. Verified with a shallow fetch: single-parent squash commits on master. The fix e2a1215 (no associated PR, message 'Fixes GHSA-95xv-3c54-c3pw') gates get() on a new _caller_can_manage_course_team(). Caveat: the impact is an account-existence oracle plus role disclosure, not data modification, and the introducing PR's tests show the empty-result-for-learners behaviour was intended, so it is a weaker authz case. Not in the global advisory DB.

cases.title: A performance refactor of AdminPermission.projects split one combined Q filter into chained .filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) calls, so read-only team members get admin rights on any project that also belongs to some admin team.
cases.where: readthedocs/core/permissions.py AdminPermission.projects(): `projects_from_teams = Project.objects.filter(teams__members=user)` then `projects_from_teams = projects_from_teams.filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS)` (or READ_ONLY_ACCESS). Chaining filters on a multi-valued relation creates two separate joins, so the membership and access conditions can match different teams.
cases.notes: Verified with a shallow fetch: both commits have a single parent. The advisory says the flaw was present from 2026-01-27 to 2026-04-20, which matches the merge date of PR #12669 (2026-01-26). The fix cc60c5d ('Merge commit from fork', the private-fork GHSA patch) rebuilds the conditions into one Q passed to a single .filter(). It only affects the organizations/teams code path (Read the Docs Business), but that code is in this public repo. Very small diff (15 lines), which makes a good hard case. Not in the global advisory DB.

cases.title: The global search PR queried MailAccount and MailRule with plain .objects.filter() behind only a model-level has_perm check, unlike the owner-aware get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() it used for tags and correspondents, so users see other users' mail accounts and rules.
cases.where: src/documents/views.py GlobalSearchView.get(): `mail_rules = MailRule.objects.filter(name__icontains=query)[:OBJECT_LIMIT] if request.user.has_perm('paperless_mail.view_mailrule')` and the same for MailAccount, while the tag/correspondent/document_type/storage_path queries in the same method use get_objects_for_user_owner_aware().
cases.notes: Found with git log -G'MailAccount.objects.filter' on views.py; single-parent squash commit. At the base, MailAccount and MailRule were already ModelWithOwner, and their own viewsets used ObjectOwnedOrGrantedPermissionsFilter, so object-level permissions existed when the search was added. The fix 9e9fc62 ('Resolve GHSA-96jx-fj7m-qh6x', direct commit on dev, no PR) swaps both queries to get_objects_for_user_owner_aware. This is the second paperless-ngx case (GHSA-386h-chg4-cfw9 is already used). Not in the global advisory DB.
